clue.text: Nobles had rattled lady with light hair

indicators.note: something rattled is shaken up, so the letters of these two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Aristocrats unsettled a fair-haired woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash blonde is a woman whose hair is a pale, greyish fair shade, so she is a lady with light hair.

clue.text: Fish hung after being topped and tailed

indicators.note: topped and tailed means having the first and last letters cut off, like a trimmed vegetable

parts.note: dangled means hung loosely

explanation.surface: A fish hung up after being prepared for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with a rod and line, so the noun-looking word is a verb here.

clue.text: Top-selling article on wrinkles maybe achieved prominence

parts.note: a hit is a best-selling record or book
the is the definite article
head lines are the creases across the forehead, an example of wrinkles

explanation.surface: A best-selling article about anti-ageing creams became famous.
explanation.definitionFit: To feature prominently in the news headlines is to gain public prominence.

clue.text: £1 added to kitty for part of rescue operation?

parts.note: L stands for pound sterling, from Latin libra
1 looks like the letter I, and I is the Roman numeral one
a kitty is a cat, a feline

explanation.surface: A pound is added to the collection fund for a rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a pool of money but is a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeline is a rope thrown to someone in danger, a key part of a rescue.

clue.text: Number Ten's brief memo

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A short memorandum from Number Ten Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten is the British prime minister's residence; here the words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a short written message, the same as a memo.

clue.text: The Observer forged new ties? Yes

indicators.note: forged means made or shaped, so the letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: A Sunday newspaper confirms it has made new links.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, but here it means a person who watches.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyewitness is someone who observes an event first-hand.

clue.text: Angel cake initially unavailable — could I help out?

indicators.note: unavailable says the letter picked out is missing, so it is dropped from the backer

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatrical show

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word cake

explanation.surface: A request for help because the angel cake has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel cake' reads as one dessert, but Angel is the backer and 'cake initially' is the C that is removed. The definition is a cryptic question: someone who makes cakes and bread might offer to help out.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who makes bread and cakes is the kind of person who might offer help when cake runs short.

clue.text: Problems with water pipes? Transport gets routed round King Street

indicators.note: the bus is routed round, going outside the other letters

parts.note: a bus is a form of transport
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Buses are diverted round a street during plumbing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Bursts are breaks in a pipe through which water escapes, a classic plumbing problem.

clue.text: Buffet serving piece of pork between slices of bread

parts.note: a knuckle is a cut of pork from the joint of the leg
a sandwich is filling placed between slices of bread

explanation.surface: A cold buffet offering a pork sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffet is not a food spread but a blow, here a punch in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A knuckle sandwich is slang for a punch, and to buffet is to strike.

clue.text: Wild animal hiding in gnarled tree, displaying coat

indicators.note: hiding in means the animal is concealed inside the other letters
gnarled means twisted, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: a dingo is a wild Australian dog

explanation.surface: A wild beast lurks in a twisted tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnarled' makes RETE from TREE, and the dingo hides inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A redingote is a long, fitted coat, originally a riding coat.

clue.text: Make a good start explaining what red card requires player to do

definitions.meaning: to get a project successfully launched or under way

definitions.text: what red card requires player to do
definitions.meaning: a player shown the red card is sent off and must leave the pitch, the ground where the game is played

explanation.surface: A football referee's dismissal described as a way of beginning well.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to start successfully; read literally it means leaving the playing field, as a sent-off footballer must.

clue.text: Puff, perhaps, previously fit

parts.note: ex means former or previously, as in ex-wife
hale means healthy and fit, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Someone who used to be fit is now short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is one example of breathing out, so the definition gives the verb by example.

clue.text: Thirty seconds to collect the post? Wrong

indicators.note: to collect means to hold something gathered inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: thirty seconds is half a minute, and half the letters of the word minute are its first three
a stake is a wooden post driven into the ground

explanation.surface: A brief pause to pick up the mail turns out to be an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thirty seconds' is half a minute, so the setter takes half of the word minute; 'the post' suggests mail but means a wooden stake.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mistaken is to be in error, so it is a synonym of wrong as an adjective.

clue.text: See him starting to pilfer, possibly

definitions.text: See him starting to pilfer, possibly

parts.words: See him starting to pilfer, possibly
parts.note: a person beginning to steal goods from a store, spotted in the act

explanation.surface: Watch a man begin stealing.
explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: the person you might see beginning to pilfer is a thief in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A store thief is someone who pilfers goods, so seeing one in action describes him.

clue.text: Assisting worker in arrears

parts.note: to be behind someone is to back or support them
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: An employee helping out who is behind with payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behindhand means being late or overdue with what is owed, the same as being in arrears.

clue.text: Unveiled, perhaps, as shameless

definitions.meaning: with the face uncovered, as when a veil is taken off

explanation.surface: Someone shows their face openly, without shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the word means with an uncovered face; figuratively it means brazen or shameless.

clue.text: Captain assigned to submarine momentarily

indicators.note: the letters are found assigned to, that is held within, the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An officer is briefly posted to a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: The captain sits hidden across the end of 'submarine' and the start of 'momentarily'; fittingly, Jules Verne's Captain Nemo commanded the submarine Nautilus.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo is the fictional commander of the Nautilus in Jules Verne's novels.

clue.text: After affair, husband keeps in control

indicators.note: After says the husband part follows the affair

parts.note: a do is a party or social affair

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the word in goes within the husband

parts.note: a mate is a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: After a fling, the husband keeps a grip on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests an extramarital fling, but it is a party, DO.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to control or hold power over.

clue.text: Study sound of musical instrument

indicators.note: sound of says the word is identified by how it is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a reed is an instrument such as a reed pipe, or a woodwind played with a reed

explanation.surface: An instruction to examine the tone of an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is to study it, especially at a British university.

clue.text: Copies tape by mistake in clergyman's office

indicators.note: letters put together by mistake are wrongly ordered, so these words must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Botched photocopying of a recording in a vicar's study.
explanation.definitionFit: The episcopate is the office or term of a bishop, a senior clergyman.

clue.text: Endless source of sherry, my boy

indicators.note: Endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Jerez in Andalusia is the town that sherry is named from
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man calls a boy his endless supply of sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy is a boy's name, one example of a boy.

clue.text: Acted as substitute, being well-informed

definitions.meaning: to stand in temporarily for someone absent
being briefed with all the details, as when someone has been told the background

explanation.surface: A stand-in who has been fully briefed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both deputised for someone and having been brought up to date with information.

clue.text: Royal power rejected medical help

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A monarch's authority turns down medical assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a crown, and by extension the royal authority it symbolises.

clue.text: Opera house introduces old time musical piece

indicators.note: introduces means brings in, so the other letters are placed inside

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Opera in New York

explanation.surface: A grand opera house brings back an old piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral composition, a musical piece.

clue.text: Almost snooze — a mistake

indicators.note: Almost means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: to go off is to fall asleep

explanation.surface: Nearly dozing off leads to an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is a silly blunder, a mistake.

clue.text: Group of sisters on a roll, entertaining one rebel? Not at all

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting or holding, so the letter for one goes inside the rest

parts.note: a convent is a community of nuns, who are called sisters
taken as written
a roll is a list of names
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Nuns on a winning streak take in a single rebel, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: The I is entertained between CONVENT and ONALIST. 'Rebel? Not at all' describes the opposite of a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sticks to convention and accepted practice is the very opposite of a rebel.

clue.text: Dark brown, mostly, and blue

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
the sky is the blue above us, poetically

explanation.surface: A description of a colour that is largely brown and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark brown' looks like the definition, but Dark alone defines and brown is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusky means darkish or shadowy, a synonym for dark.

clue.text: Plunders recent report

parts.note: to rifle is to search and plunder
hot means very recent, as in hot news

explanation.surface: Looting is the latest news story.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp sound of a gun firing, such as the bang of a fired rifle.
